entries.title: Margin notes say where a quotation comes from
entries.body: When a passage quotes, alludes to or names something and the article does not say where it is from, the margin can show a short note headed Origin that does. These are the only margin notes that come from the AI's own memory rather than the article, so each one is labelled "AI memory, unchecked", and the AI is told to stay silent when it is not sure.

entries.title: Refused paper links can use a free copy
entries.body: For supported paper addresses, when the journal's site refuses to let the app in or shows a bot check, Spideryarn looks for an open-access full text of the same paper in Europe PMC, a free library of research papers, and uses that instead. If it finds none, you see the original refusal, as before. Links to Europe PMC articles can also be added directly.

entries.title: Pages saved with the bookmarklet keep their address
entries.body: A page you save with the bookmarklet and upload from here on keeps the address it came from, shown as a "Saved from" link at the top of the article. Pasting that address later finds the article already in your library rather than adding it again. Spideryarn never visits that address itself.

entries.title: Margin citations show what the cited work says
entries.body: Opening a "Cites" note in the margin also shows the short, checked note on what the cited work says, taken from its abstract, when there is one. It is the same note the Sources panel shows, so you can see what a citation says without leaving the passage you are reading.

entries.title: Shared articles show visitors what you see
entries.body: People reading an article you have shared see its front and back matter, such as the authors and references, folded away as you do. In Skim, they also stop at the paper's figures along the route, where before they walked the passages only and met no figures.

entries.title: The topics row starts with six topics
entries.body: Above your library and the public library, the row of topics shows the first six rather than twelve, plus any you have selected. "All topics" opens the rest, and stays available while the row is open, so you can close it again before clearing a filter.
